summary: Two fixed red range lights at Darnley Point, PEI, that marked the way into Malpeque Harbour from 1889; keepers included the Morrisons and G. W. J. Wiggins; status disputed.

light.note: Front light. Rear light focal plane 21 m (LH).

structures.note: Cedar-shingled, painted white with red trim; corner boards and wooden gallery brackets (LH, register).
Iron gallery brackets, no corner boards (LH).

access.note: Lighthouse Road is private; site and tower closed.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (owner); the site manager is private (Rowlett).

events.note: Nine petitioners ask for a second light on Fish Island and two lights on Darnley Point.
Darnley Point range lights established; each a lantern on a 9.1 m mast over a shed.
Slatwork from the Brighton Beach light fixed to the masts for daytime visibility.
Open-frame towers with enclosed lanterns replace the masts, under Milton Walsh.
Works account for year ended 30 June 1900: a $10 item for moving the back tower at Darnley point; no further detail.
Fiscal 1916-17 works table: moving range lights to new sites at Darnley point, by contract. Column alignment is by position.
Rowlett gives 1922 with a question mark for the present towers.
Lights electrified; the keeper's post becomes a caretaker's (LH).
Registered under the PEI Historic Places Protection Act, 12 July 2012.
Rowlett: inactive since 2018. Lighthouse Friends says the red lights are still displayed; undated.

corrections.why: The 1961 date in Rowlett belongs to the Fish Island light (station established 1876), not the Darnley Point range, which LH and the register date to 1889. LH dates the electrification to 1962.
LH gives focal planes for each light (12.6 m front, 21 m rear). The single 14.0 m figure matches neither and comes from OSM.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rowlett dates the present towers to 1922 with a question mark. Wikipedia repeats 1922 but is not a source here. The official reports read in the corpus (to 1924) do not name a Darnley tower build, so the date stays unconfirmed. LH's towers of 1897 were later enclosed.
Rowlett says inactive since 2018. LH says the red lights are still displayed, undated. Unresolved; see notes.
The register spells G. W. J. Wiggans; the 1905 lightkeepers' list prints Wiggins, G. W. J against Darnley Point Range.
LH gives 440 m (1,444 ft) for the rear light's distance; the register gives about 1,444 ft. LH's 1908 description gives 409 m. The 1,444 ft figure is the one consistent across sources.

notes_for_editor: Status is disputed: Rowlett says inactive since 2018, while LH says the red lights are still displayed (undated; LH page may be older). The record's 'active' and the 2018 'deactivated' event need a current Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights check; NOTMAR's list was not readable here. The 1922 build date is Rowlett's, with a question mark; no corpus report confirms it. The 1917 contract line was matched to the Darnley point row by position in the OCR, and the page image (scan 44, printed 37) confirms it: 'Moving range lights to new sites', How performed 'Contract', contractor C. Morrison, $25. The contractor is not linked to the keeper Cornelius Morrison. The 1900 'moving back tower' item is confirmed on the page image (scan 76, printed 61: Darnley point, $10.00 in the minor-repairs table); its meaning is not stated. The 1905 'Wiggins, G. W. J' line is confirmed on the image (scan 347, printed 266, same row as Darnley Point Range, appointed Oct. 15, 1896). Fact-check 2026-10-28: the story now states the 1922 date as Rowlett's only, does not say the open frames were the present towers, and drops the 'keeper's post became a caretaker's' inference. The register's 'Department of Transport design' for the 1897 towers is anachronistic for the period (the department then was Marine and Fisheries) and is not used. Named keepers after 1960 (Champion) are named only as LH names him. No wrecks or rescues are tied to these lights in the sources read. Wikipedia (1922, still active) was not cited. The 1912-13 keeper lists print G. W. Wiggins without a station and were not used.
